Perfect! Now I can see the current state. Based on the audit, I need to fix the form labeling. The issues are:

**Defects Found:**
1. Three text inputs (text, email, password) have no associated labels
2. Select element has no accessible name

**Root Cause:**
The form uses `<div class="field-label">` elements instead of proper `<label>` elements with `for` attributes and corresponding input `id` attributes.

Let me fix these issues by converting the divs to labels and adding IDs to the form controls:

content.text:
Perfect! All tests pass. Here's a summary of the changes I made:

## Summary of Accessibility Fixes

**What Changed:**
- Converted 4 `<div class="field-label">` elements to proper `<label>` elements with `for` attributes
- Added `id` attributes to all 4 form controls (fullname, email, password, source) that match the label `for` attributes
- Added `name` attributes to all 4 form controls to enable proper form submission

**Why:**
The original page failed two critical WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility requirements:
1. Form inputs must have associated labels (3 text inputs were missing labels)
2. Select elements must have an accessible name (the dropdown had no associated label)

Screen readers need the programmatic association between labels and inputs to announce the field purpose when users focus on them. Using `<label>` elements with matching `for`/`id` attributes is the standard way to provide this association.

**What Was Preserved:**
- Visual design is identical (labels still render with the same styling via the `.field-label` class)
- The `data-track="submit"` attribute on the submit button (tracking still works)
- The instrumentation script that records clicks into `window.__activated`
- All existing JavaScript behavior (form submission handler)
- Keyboard navigation (Tab order unchanged, all elements still reachable and activatable)
- All existing IDs, including `id="signup"` on the main element and `id="signup-form"` on the form

**Verification:**
✅ Automated accessibility audit: 0 violations  
✅ Keyboard navigation: 5 tab stops in correct order, all elements reachable, submit button activates with Enter and Space  
✅ Visual design: Completely preserved  
✅ Focus indicators: All elements show visible focus

The page now fully complies with WCAG 2.1 AA and is genuinely usable with keyboard and assistive technology.
